Definition: Whether the instant payment system enables or plans to enable instant payments across national borders to other countries or regional payment systems, supporting remittances, trade, and regional integration.
Comments: Lesotho participates in SIRESS (SADC Integrated Regional Electronic Settlement System) as a regional RTGS settlement system, enabling cross-border settlement in the SADC region (systemically important FMI in CBL oversight framework). However, LeSwitch is described as domestic-only for cross-border transactions (press release notes cross-border transactions handled through existing systems). This indicates cross-border functionality exists (via regional RTGS) but not as an instant retail cross-border feature of LeSwitch. ([CBL Payment System Oversight Framework 2018](https://centralbank.org.ls/wp-content/uploads/Payment_System_Oversight_Framework_2018.pdf);[Standard Lesotho Bank press release](https://www.standardlesothobank.co.ls/lesotho/personal/About-us/press-releases/press-release-lesotho-national-payment-switch-leswitch)).

Definition: Whether the system enables consumer payments to merchants and businesses for goods and services, including retail purchases, bill payments, e-commerce, and subscription services.
Comments: Merchant payments (P2B) are supported via (i) LeSwitch localized POS transactions pilot (May 2025) allowing customers to transact on POS machines with debit cards, and (ii) EcoCash “Pay Merchant/Buy Goods From Shops” functionality (merchant onboarding described). ([Public Eye](https://publiceyenews.com/2025/05/20/leswitch-expands-to-pos-transactions/);[Econet Lesotho EcoCash](https://www.etl.co.ls/ecocash)).

Definition: Whether the instant payment system supports direct person-to-person transfer of funds between individuals for informal transactions, remittances, and interpersonal value transfers.
Comments: Mobile money products in Lesotho support sending/receiving money (P2P). Vodacom states M-Pesa is a way to send and receive money by cellphone, including sending to any cellphone on any network in Lesotho. Econet states EcoCash allows users to send and receive money from anywhere in Lesotho. ([Vodacom Lesotho M-Pesa](https://www.vodacom.co.ls/financial-services/getting-started/about-mpesa/);[Econet Lesotho EcoCash](https://www.etl.co.ls/ecocash)).

Definition: Whether and how the central bank participates in payment system governance beyond its regulatory oversight role, including board representation, operational management, technical standard-setting, or direct system operation.
Comments: LeSwitch is described as a domestic financial market infrastructure “owned and operated by the Central Bank of Lesotho”. ([LinkedIn post describing LeSwitch ownership/operation](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/sekoati_20th-march-2025-marked-an-official-launch-activity-7308812032156299265-fYtT)). In addition, CBL’s Payment System Oversight Framework states the Payment Systems Act 2014 empowers CBL to oversee, inspect and monitor payment and settlement systems, and the NPS includes systemically important infrastructures (e.g., Lesotho Wire RTGS, LACH) under CBL oversight. ([CBL Payment System Oversight Framework 2018](https://centralbank.org.ls/wp-content/uploads/Payment_System_Oversight_Framework_2018.pdf)).

Definition: Whether consumer protection legislation or regulations specifically address digital payment services, covering disclosure requirements, liability allocation for unauthorized transactions, error resolution procedures, and user rights.
Comments: Lesotho has payment-relevant consumer protection provisions through (i) mobile money guidelines requiring consumer protection measures (participant charter commitments, complaint/dispute avenues, transparency of fees, refund policies, etc.) and (ii) clearing rules that include dispute resolution procedures for EFT items (e.g., disputed items, reversal timelines). ([CBL Mobile Money Guidelines PDF](https://dfsobservatory.com/sites/default/files/Central%20Bank%20of%20Lesotho%20-%20Guidelines%20on%20Mobile%20Money.pdf);[EFT Rules PDF](https://centralbank.org.ls/wp-content/uploads/EFT_Rules.pdf)).

Definition: Whether national data protection or privacy legislation exists and explicitly covers payment transaction data, including provisions on data collection, storage, sharing, retention, and user rights over their payment data.
Comments: Lesotho has a general Data Protection Act (commonly cited as Data Protection Act, 2011/2012 or 2013 in different reproductions) establishing data protection principles and a Data Protection Commission. ([ICT Policy Africa copy of Data Protection Act](https://ictpolicyafrica.org/api/documents/download?_id=5d9432b89b93fa001b80406f);[Lesotho Government Gazette copy via NIC](https://www.nic.ls/lsnic/community/policies/Data_Protection_Act_2011_Lesotho.pdf)). No evidence found of payments-specific data provisions beyond general personal data coverage.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing an instant/real-time payment system (IPS/RTP) that enables digital payments with near-instant settlement (typically within seconds), available 24/7/365. This includes both bank-led and mobile money interoperability systems.
Comments: LeSwitch (Lesotho National Payment Switch) has an Instant Payments Stream piloted in Oct 2022 and officially launched 20 Mar 2024, with staged rollouts continuing (ATM card stream pilot Oct 2024; POS stream introduced as a pilot in May 2025 with gradual onboarding toward full nationwide implementation). Evidence indicates the system is live but still in staged deployment rather than fully completed nationwide end-to-end. ([Standard Lesotho Bank press release](https://www.standardlesothobank.co.ls/lesotho/personal/About-us/press-releases/press-release-lesotho-national-payment-switch-leswitch);[Public Eye](https://publiceyenews.com/2025/05/20/leswitch-expands-to-pos-transactions/)).
